project_name: US POP Tech Order Governance and Official Logistics Switch
reason: [Background] Some US POP merchants used unpaid postage labels (UPO) to avoid shipping costs and gain unfair price advantages. This led to unhealthy competition and serious user experience issues once USPS stopped deliveries and charged customers. The platform needed decisive governance to restore fairness and protect user trust.[Challenges]Governance could impact short-term GMV but inaction would harm user experience.UPO detection relied on delayed and limited USPS signals, making suspected cases harder to handle.Policy rollout timing conflicted with holiday and Black Friday preparations.[Strategy] A three-phase, tiered rollout ultimately restricted 3PL usage across merchants:Phase 1: Full 3PL ban for confirmed UPO violators.Phase 2: Restrictions of seller shipping with USPS for high-risk merchants.Phase 3: POP-wide 3PL restriction (except those not accepted by TT shipping)[Impact]UPO signals reduced from 3,900 weekly orders to zero.Postage-related cancellation rate dropped from 22.34% to 4.63%.190K merchants transitioned from 3PL in Q4.Official logistics penetration rose from 13.5% to 92.1% (+78.6pp).Ultra-low-price competition declined significantly.The initiative restored fair competition, protected user trust during Black Friday, and accelerated official logistics scale and capability upgrades.[Reflection] Early warning signals appeared in July, but action was delayed due to GMV concerns. Going forward, risks must be identified and addressed earlier to better balance growth and user experience.
department: Supply Chain and Logistics-Business Analysis and Data Science

project_name: SEA Machine and Logistics Cost Optimization Initiative
reason: The core optimization focus of algorithms and services has been GMV growth, while the SEA business simultaneously places strong emphasis on profitability. Cost savings can be converted 100% into incremental profit. In 2025, recommendation, search, logistics algorithms, architecture, backend, DS, and operations teams worked closely together to tackle two key cost drivers: machine cost and logistics cost. The initiative delivered annualized cost savings of $119.57M, becoming a major profit engine beyond core GMV growth.Cross-functional collaboration broke down the business–tech barriers to drive cost optimization:On machine resource optimization, the algorithm team analyzed traffic value and feature importance, while the architecture team implemented caching and compute scheduling improvements. Together they optimized inference allocation, removed low-contribution features, and eliminated redundant services and data, saving $35.15M annually.On the backend side, architecture improved core component utilization (TCE 30% → 42%), completed public cloud migration, and enhanced peak elasticity, reducing rates by 35% and saving $45.00M annually.On logistics cost, traffic algorithms integrated Zone and same-island factors into recommendation strategies, reducing logistics costs in ID/VN by 8.41% and saving $12.52M annually.Logistics dispatch algorithms were upgraded and extended to instant and same-day scenarios, delivering $26.90M in annual savings.This cost optimization initiative aligned with SEA’s transition from scale-driven growth to high-quality growth, striking a sustainable balance between expansion and profitability while establishing a reusable methodology and cross-team collaboration model for future efficiency improvements.
